names.notify.title: Notifications
names.notify.show.for: Show a notification on this computer for:
names.notify.nothing.looking: Nothing shows for the chat or post you're looking at. Closing the window keeps Weave running in the tray, so notifications keep coming; quit from the tray icon.
names.notify.blocked: Notifications are blocked for Weave in your system or browser settings.
names.notify.test.title: Weave notifications work
names.notify.test.text: This is how messages, requests and project activity will show.
names.rules.title: Rules
names.rules.hint: · the most specific one wins: a person over a place, a board over its project; kept with Unread, so all your devices count alike
names.rules.default: Without a rule, messages to you count (a number next to the chat or place, until you open it) and the kinds above notify.
names.origin.weave.title: Made by Weave: checked against what this Weave ships
names.origin.release.title: A release of {project}, version {tag}
names.hints.about: Numbers, tints and signs next to places and on messages come from these, worked out on your Weave; what you open counts no more on all your devices.
names.hints.take.in: Take in {what}? It shows counts, colors and signs next to your places and messages, and runs inside Weave with no key and no network.
names.hints.newest: the newest hint service p/{project} released
names.hints.take.from: Take one in from a project…
names.service.newer.out: {tag} is out: it runs only with your yes.
names.marks.badge.unknown: This node doesn't know that badge (or it moved on to someone else).
names.marks.title: Marks
names.marks.about: Mark services show what they say next to names, everywhere you look; hover a mark to see who says so. Projects and communities can pin their own, shown only in them.
names.marks.take.in: Take in {what}? Weave runs exactly that release over what your Weave holds, with no key and no network, and shows what it says next to names everywhere you look.
names.marks.newest: the newest mark service p/{project} released
names.marks.fromweave.note: Without it, a look-alike of Weave can’t be told apart at a glance.
names.update.title: Updates
names.update.ready: Weave {version} is ready to install. Restarting ends the Weave daemon and any weave commands or agents using it; they start again with the new version.
names.update.available.title: Weave {version} is available
names.update.available.text: You have Weave {current}. Weave {version} came out{when}{announced}. Weave is still 0.x: please update, so everyone speaks the same version.
names.update.announced: , announced in the Weave project by its maintainers
names.update.browser.note: New versions are installed by the desktop app; the browser preview only says when there is one.
names.update.standing.ready: Weave {version} is downloaded and checked: restart to install it.
names.update.auto: Download new versions in the background, then offer a restart
names.update.auto.note: Weave installs only a file whose SHA-256 is the one a maintainer of the Weave project signed with the release, and installs it when you click Restart to update, never behind your back. Off: Weave says when a new version is out, and gets it when you ask.
names.update.why.development: This Weave runs from its source: start the new version yourself.
names.update.why.managed: This computer gets new versions from its IT.
names.update.why.store: This Weave comes from the Microsoft Store, which updates it.
names.update.why.per-machine: This Weave was installed for everyone on this computer: your IT installs new versions.
names.update.why.unsigned: This Weave isn't signed with a Developer ID yet, so macOS won't let it replace itself: download the new one.
names.update.why.not-installed: This Weave isn't installed in a way it can replace: download the new one.
names.onboard.intro: Your hub, your keys, your friends. Your identity is created on this computer and never leaves it.
names.onboard.name: What should people call you?
names.onboard.words.title: Your recovery words
names.onboard.words.write: Write these 24 words down on paper, in order. They are shown only now.
names.onboard.words.why: They are your identity: with them you set up another computer, replace a stolen key and rotate your keys. Weave never stores them. Keep them away from this computer, from chats and from AI agents: whoever has them is you.
names.onboard.words.wrote: I wrote them down and put them somewhere safe
names.onboard.company.welcome: Welcome, {name}. Your account belongs to {company}: it keeps it safe and can set it up on a new computer, so there are no words to write down.
names.onboard.company.signed: You stay signed in with your company account; Weave renews it by itself. Your company's projects and groups appear as soon as the company has let you in.
names.onboard.company.title: Set up your company account
names.onboard.company.intro: Your company sets up your Weave account. You sign in with your company account in your browser; there are no recovery words to keep.
names.onboard.company.managed: Your company has set this computer up for its Weave already.
names.onboard.company.link: The enrollment link from your company
names.onboard.company.waiting: Waiting for the sign-in in your browser…
names.onboard.restore.title: Restore Weave on this computer
names.onboard.restore.done: This computer is now one of your devices
names.onboard.restore.intro: Type your 24 recovery words. Keep another of your devices, or a friend who follows you, online: this computer fetches your identity from them.
names.company.belongs: This account belongs to {name}. The company keeps it safe and can set it up on a new computer.
names.company.belongs.signed: This account belongs to {name} and is signed in as {account}. The company keeps it safe and can set it up on a new computer.
names.company.renews: Weave renews the sign-in by itself.
names.company.signin.again.when: Sign in again when it runs out.
names.company.vouches.until: The company vouches for you until {until, date, medium}, {until, time, short}.
names.company.vouches.once: The company vouches for you once it has checked the sign-in.
names.company.signin.title: Opens your company's sign-in in the browser
names.keys.since: Last time you trusted it (empty: from now on)
names.keys.replace.encryption: Also replace my encryption key (if it may have leaked)
names.keys.words.once: The words go to your own node only, are used once and are not stored.
names.agent.may.title: What {name} may do
names.agent.may.intro: Everything {name} writes is signed with its own key and shows as “you · {name}”. It can only sign what you tick here.
names.agent.revoke.ask: Revoke the agent {name}? It can't sign anything from now on.
names.keystore.move.ask: Keep the key to your keys in {name}? Weave then opens only with it{yubikey}. If it's lost or replaced, you set Weave up again from your recovery words, or your company does.
names.keystore.move.yubikey: plugged in (touch it if it blinks)
names.keystore.moved: The key is now kept by {name}
names.nodes.about: A server, NAS or home cluster that keeps your spaces and hosts your rooms while your computers are off. It gets a key of its own that only hosts rooms (it can't post or change anything for you), and your spaces' keys, but not your direct chats. On it, run weave-server pair and paste its request here.
names.node.revoke.ask: Revoke the always-on node {name}? It stops hosting your rooms, and what it signs from now on counts nowhere.
names.node.linked: Linked {name}. On the node, run weave-server join with this answer:
names.key.replace.title: Replace this device key
names.key.revoke.title: Revoke device
names.key.replace.intro: This computer gets a fresh key; anything signed with the old one after the time you choose becomes void.
names.key.revoke.intro: Everything {name} signed after the time you choose becomes void, on every node.
names.keys.forked: A key of yours was seen signing in two places at once: it may be stolen, or your Weave folder was copied to another computer. Revoke it from the time you last trusted it.
names.keys.unprotected.long: Your keys are not protected by the operating system here: anyone who copies your Weave folder can use them. Weave found no keystore it can use{where}.
names.keys.sealed: Your keys are sealed, and the key to them is kept by {name}: a copy of your Weave folder can't be opened on another computer or by another user.
names.keys.other.computer.company: To use Weave on another computer, ask {company} to set it up.
names.keys.other.computer.words: To use Weave on another computer, set it up from your recovery words.
names.keepers.about: Friends keep a sealed copy of your own space, your direct chats and your small groups, so that you can get them back with your recovery words even if every device is lost. They can't read it or tell what it is.
names.keepers.none: no keeper yet: you need friends (people you follow who follow you back)
names.keepers.you.keep: You keep {mb} MB for friends (at most {max} MB).
names.identity.company.holds: {company} holds this identity's recovery words. For a new computer, run weave recover-request there and give the request to one of {company}'s admins.
names.identity.recoverable: Protected by your recovery words. Your root key was rotated {n, plural, one {# time} other {# times}}; your words already cover the next one.
names.identity.old: This identity was made before recovery words existed: it can't rotate keys or add devices. Creating a new identity gives you both.
names.keys.rotate.intro: Your root key moves on to the next one your words hold; the old one stops counting. Do this if you think your root key leaked, or now and then.
names.devices.each.signs: Each computer signs with its own key.
names.devices.other.company: For another computer, ask {company}; don't copy your Weave folder.
names.devices.other.words: To use Weave on another computer, choose “I already use Weave” there and type your words; don't copy your Weave folder.

names.join.onchain.wallet: Paying in {symbol} goes from your own wallet, so {creator} knows the payment is yours.

names.tier.onchain.price: Give the price in USDC, like 5 or 2.50
names.tier.gumroad.not.yet: {name} is saved, but not on Gumroad yet: Edit it to try again
names.tier.gumroad.unpublished: {name} is on Gumroad, not published yet: {warning}
names.tier.edit.title: Edit {name}
names.tier.new.title: New tier
names.tier.benefits.placeholder:
Supporter lounge
Early builds of my projects
names.tier.auto: Let people in automatically (for free tiers)
names.tier.ways.about: Offer one or more; supporters pick theirs when they join. Nothing ticked: they pay you the way you agree on, and you let them in.
names.tier.gumroad.option: Gumroad: card, PayPal; Gumroad is the seller
names.gumroad.make: Make the product on Gumroad for me
names.gumroad.make.new: Make a new product on Gumroad
names.gumroad.keep.linked: Keep the product it is linked to, or link another
names.gumroad.token.howto: In Gumroad: Settings → Advanced → Applications, create an application (any name and redirect URI), then Generate access token. Weave uses it once and doesn't keep it.
names.gumroad.allow: Allow Weave in your browser, then come back.
names.gumroad.makes: Weave makes a monthly membership at this price on Gumroad, with license keys, and publishes it. Supporters buy there and send you the key from their receipt; your Weave lets them in and renews each month while they pay. Keep Weave running so it can.
names.gumroad.product.id: Product ID (Gumroad: the product's settings, or its page's “License key” section)
names.gumroad.variant: Gumroad tier that gives this one (if the membership has several)
names.gumroad.linked.howto: In Gumroad, make it a membership and turn on Generate a unique license key per sale. Supporters buy there and send you the key from their receipt; your Weave checks it with Gumroad, lets them in and renews each month while they pay. Keep Weave running so it can.
names.tier.usdc.option: USDC: from a wallet, straight to you (test network)
names.tier.payto.placeholder: 0x… (link your wallet, or give an address)
names.tier.onchain.about: Empty: your linked wallet. Supporters pay from their linked wallet; your Weave reads the payment on {chain} and lets them in. Keep Weave running so it can. (To divide payments among a project's makers, give its split contract here: weave treasury split, once the project's payments are on.)
names.tier.is.group: A tier is a group: members get its chat and every project you invite it into (in the project's Settings). Memberships give access, never votes.
names.tier.remove.ask: Take {name} off your hub? Members keep it until their grants run out.
names.tiers.offer.about: Offer memberships, Patreon-style: supporters get a lounge and the projects you open to them.
names.tiers.support.none: You don't support anyone yet. Creators offer tiers on their hub.
names.request.valid.months: valid, {n, plural, one {# month} other {# months}}

names.session.rename.title: Rename {name}, or change what it is about
names.session.drag.link: Drag to the other side to link
names.session.new.hint: In a folder, with a job; or drop a project here
names.session.unlink: Unlink: {session} no longer takes work from {project}
names.sessions.how.linking.text: Link a session to a project by dragging from one side to the other: it then takes that project's work items, from you (Ctrl+click) and from your daily driver. Click a line to unlink. A dot marks the project a session is working in now.
names.sessions.follow.title: Reads the agent's answers in {dir} and the Claude app's log, on this computer only
names.sessions.none: No Claude Code sessions here yet. Turn on Follow Claude Code to see them.
names.session.name.about: A session names itself once, and goes by “name · about” everywhere in Weave. The name is permanent for the session: only you change it here. Its title in the Claude app is the session's to set{now}.
names.session.name.field: Name (one short word nobody around you has)
names.session.about.field: About (one line on what it specializes in)
names.session.folder.pick: Folder for the new session (Claude Code works in it)
names.session.new.title: New Claude Code session
names.session.first.message: First message (optional; it waits in the text box, not sent)
names.session.follow.first: Turn on Follow Claude Code first: Weave gives the session its job once it sees it in the Claude app.
names.session.not.seen: not seen in the Claude app yet
names.work.on.title: Work on “{title}”
names.work.who.takes: Who takes it? It goes on top of that session's stack, and the session opens in Claude with the message in its text box.
names.work.where.last.title: Its latest session, or the daily driver for your desk
names.status.peers: {n, plural, one {# peer connected} other {# peers connected}}
names.status.older.title: Peers on an older Weave can't sync with you. They get a message in each shared group asking them to update, and nothing else.
names.status.newer: {n} on a newer Weave: update to sync
names.status.newer.title: Peers on a newer Weave can't sync with you until you update.
